subject: RApache default plot behavior seems suboptimal

messages.author: b75df6bb42949437
messages.subject: RApache default plot behavior seems suboptimal
parts:
Hello all,

I am new to both R and Rapache, but I've been programming for 10 plus years, and spend some of that time as a unix admin. I'm a little concerned about the default behavior of rapache plotting.

From what I can tell, if you don't specify the output, plotting has a sane default for most R implementations. For the RScript console, it writes a PDF to the working directory. For the R GUI it pops up a window. For RStudio, there is a window that displays plots and has arrows for navigation between them. Rapache. seems to put a default PDF in the directory where the R script lives. Generally, speaking Apache doesn't have access to that directory, as it shouldn't. The workarounds are simple, call CarioPNG on a temp file, and pass that file to sendBin(), or I can (possibly?) also use a memory stream.

It seems that a memory stream, or a memory mapped file that gets deleted at the end of the transaction would be a cleaner way to go for the default. Does that make sense? Is that feasible?

Thanks,
Justin

messages.author: 25a4f5811cd7d59e
messages.subject: Re: RApache default plot behavior seems suboptimal
parts:
The Cairo package does have an undocumented way of grabbing a png plot's memory context before turning off an open device, and there's another png package (who's name escapes me) that will allow you translate that context to an in-memory png. But this doesn't work for any other graphics devices supported by Cairo.

Also rApache is a low level application layer, and I'm still waiting for someone to step up with bold opinions (including defaults for creating plots) and write an R web application framework on top of Rook/rApache. OpenCPU is one such framework that has done this for web services, but there ought to be a Django or Rails equivalent.

messages.author: b75df6bb42949437
messages.subject: Re: RApache default plot behavior seems suboptimal
parts:
Jeffrey,

Let me start with some bold opinions. I personally don't want a framework. I want scripts to return JSON, xls, CSV, or images. I want a very simple set of rules to give to an analyst so that they an write scripts that will work on the console,, RStudio, and in RApache. I generally want it to be hard for analysts that don't understand web apps to want to do something that would be bad in the eyes of a traditional web programmer (insecure, non-performant, etc. Maybe I'll one day want something  like NancyFX, but for now one script per method is fine.

So some suggestions that I can at least turn into github issues:
* Can plotting by default not go to the script folder? Even if that simply means it goes to a temp file and there is a builtin variable with the temp file name?
* Can there be a new Handler where the plotting device is set to spew out to the http response body, and STDOUT text be discarded? I think that means the response body would be cached until dev.off is called.
* Can there be a new directive called REvalOnRequest that behaves like REvalOnStartup, but runs before a script is run? This will be useful if people want to do exotic things with plotting (e.g memory mapped files).
* Can the default plot be a svg
* Can plotting a second graph when the output method is not a multipage tiff or pdf cause an error to appear in the http log?

I don't code a lot of C, but I can try my hand at the first request at least. That seems straight forward.

Thanks
Justin

Hi Justin,

Jeroen also authored a security-related package that is let you run R codes in AppArmor profiles/hats: https://github.com/jeroenooms/RAppArmor

On the other hand, as you mentioned "particular scripts", I also mention my sandbocR package, that can parse all R code sent by your users and does not let them run blacklisted functions. A whitelist-method could be created easily there also, please let me know if you'd be interested in such parser: https://github.com/Rapporter/sandboxR

Best.
Gergely
